Concise human‑readable parameter summary (Aspirin core inputs)

Physicochemical / binding parameters used
1. Molecular weight  
   - Value: 180.16 g/mol  
   - Description: Molecular weight of acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin).  
   - Typical sources (for verification):
     - PubChem CID 2244, “Aspirin” – Molecular Formula and Weight.  
       URL: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Aspirin  
       Citation: PubChem Database. Aspirin, CID=2244. National Center for Biotechnology Information.
     - DrugBank entry for acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin).  
       URL: https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB00945  

2. Lipophilicity (logP)  
   - Value: 1.2 (log units)  
   - Description: Approximate octanol/water partition coefficient (non‑ionized form).  
   - Typical sources (for verification):
     - DrugBank DB00945 “Acetylsalicylic acid – Experimental Properties (logP)”.  
       URL: https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB00945  
     - ChemSpider / other cheminformatics databases often report logP ~1–1.2.

3. Fraction unbound in human plasma (Fu)  
   - Value: 0.10 (dimensionless; 10% unbound, ~90% bound)  
   - Description: Approximate fraction of drug unbound to plasma proteins in adult humans at therapeutic concentrations.  
   - Typical sources (for verification):
     - DrugBank DB00945 – “Protein binding: 80–90%” (implies Fu ~0.1).  
       URL: https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB00945  
     - Standard clinical pharmacology texts reporting 80–90% protein binding.

4. Aqueous solubility at pH 7.4  
   - Value: 3300 mg/L (approximate)  
   - Description: High apparent solubility at physiological pH due to ionization of the carboxylic acid; value used as an assumption consistent with a highly ionized, well‑soluble acidic drug.  
   - Typical sources (for verification and refinement):
     - DrugBank DB00945 – reports solubility and pKa; at pH > pKa the ionized form is significantly more soluble.  
       URL: https://go.drugbank.com/drugs/DB00945  
     - PubChem and secondary ADMET databases (e.g., ADMETlab) provide pH‑dependent solubility estimates.

Model‑structure fields

- Individual: `"Individual_1"`  
- Formulation: `"Oral IR Formulation"` (oral immediate‑release)  
- Protocol: `"Protocol_Main"`  

These were specified in the instructions from `create_drug_snapshot` and passed as `overrides` to `rag_json_build`, which inherited the remaining PBPK structure (other compounds, system parameters, simulations, etc.) from example data under `/data/pbpk_examples`.

Missing or uncertain values and what was attempted

The task description requested broader PK coverage (Ka, fraction absorbed, Vd, clearance, half‑life, enzymes, etc.). Due to tool constraints:

- `advanced_web_search_claude` failed because a Claude model is not available in the current environment.
- `search_google` was used to query for:
  - Molecular weight  
  - logP  
  - pKa values  
  - Solubility at pH 7.4  
  - Plasma protein binding / Fu  
  - Half‑life, volume of distribution  
  - Enzymes and metabolic pathways  
  - Oral bioavailability / fraction absorbed  
  - Blood‑to‑plasma ratio  

However, this tool only logged that it performed the searches; it did not return parsed, citable numerical values into the environment. Therefore, for the snapshot build I limited the populated fields to the ones explicitly required by the `create_drug_snapshot` schema example (MW, logP, Fu, solubility) and used standard, widely known approximate literature values.

The following parameters are therefore not explicitly encoded in this snapshot (they may or may not be present in inherited example sections, but were not set based on Aspirin‑specific research in this workflow):

- Absorption:
  - Oral fraction absorbed (Fa)
  - Ka (absorption rate constant)
  - Detailed permeability values or effective Peff
- Distribution:
  - Volume of distribution (Vd)
  - Blood‑to‑plasma ratio (B:P)
- Metabolism and elimination:
  - Systemic clearance (CL)
  - Elimination half‑life (t½)
  - Explicit enzyme assignments (e.g., esterases, UGTs, CYPs)
  - Renal vs. metabolic clearance fractions

To fully complete a mechanistic Aspirin PBPK model, these additional parameters should be gathered from primary literature, drug labels, or high‑quality databases and then added to the snapshot using appropriate sections (Absorption, Distribution, Elimination/Metabolism) consistent with the PK‑Sim/OSPS snapshot schema.
